Mica (People Ops): Morning team — heads-up on a small bundle of policy updates that go live May 15. TL;DR: travel receipt rules clarified, international travel cap adjusted, parental leave pilot expanded, PTO rollover tweaked, and a quick code-of-conduct ack reminder. Full policy doc here: https://redwood.internal/policies/ops-updates-2026 :eyes:

Jordan A.: Quick — does spouse airfare count under the travel cap if booked on the same itinerary?

PeopleOps-Bot: Auto-reply: Companion travel is generally not covered unless explicitly business-related (recruiting, relocation). See "Companions" in the travel section: https://redwood.internal/policies/ops-updates-2026#companions :robot_face:

Olivia (HR): Confirming — spouse/partner airfare is only eligible in narrow cases (relocation, critical recruiting travel, or pre-approved exec travel). For family travel during personal time, that's out-of-pocket. If in doubt, submit the expense and tag HR for pre-approval.

Devin (Eng Mgr): For planning: how does this affect team offsites? We book mixed itineraries and sometimes cover partner dinners.

Mica (People Ops): Offsites are handled via the offsite budget line (separate from individual travel caps). The individual travel cap applies to reimbursements on personal claims. If you're planning a team offsite, file an offsite budget request to finance with estimated totals; we'll exempt approved offsite expenses from the per-person cap.

Jordan A.: Got it. On parental leave — what changed exactly? My partner and I are expecting later this year.

Olivia (HR): Parental leave pilot (Q3 hires onward): primary caregivers will be eligible for 18 weeks fully paid leave (pilot for 12 months), and secondary caregivers keep 6 weeks fully paid. We're running this as a pilot to gather data on uptake and operational impacts. Eligibility, notice periods, and phased return support are in the doc.

Mica (People Ops): A few quick operational bullets:
- Effective date: May 15 for travel/PTO changes; parental leave pilot enrollment open June 1 for eligible hires.
- PTO rollover: you can carry over up to 10 days to the next year; anything beyond will be flagged for use or payout per your manager/comp plan.
- Code of conduct: no policy text change, but annual acknowledgment is required by May 31. We'll send reminders.

Jordan A.: Is there a form for parental leave so we can start the paperwork?

PeopleOps-Bot: Leave intake form: https://redwood.internal/forms/leave-intake. Workflow: submit -> HR review -> manager notification -> scheduling conversation.

Alan (Finance): Quick note on receipts: we now accept digital invoices and e-tickets as primary proof. Please attach PDFs from the vendor or airline. Screenshots of card charges alone will be rejected. Example minimal claim: 

```
Expense: Intl flight
Amount: $1,320.45
Receipt: flight_2026-05-12.pdf
```

Alan (Finance): Also, international per-trip cap adjusted to $1,500 (was $1,200). Luxury upgrades must be pre-approved and will be deducted from your personal reimbursement if not approved.

Mica (People Ops): We'll host a 30-minute AMA next Tuesday at 11:00am in #all-hands to walk through examples and answer questions. If you can't make it, we'll post the recording and an FAQ.

Olivia (HR): Please also remember to complete the annual Code of Conduct ack by May 31. If you already did it last month, you're all set — thanks. :raised_hands:

Jordan A.: Appreciate the clarity. One last thing — timeline for manager approvals on leave?

Olivia (HR): Request at least 8 weeks' notice for planned parental leave. We'll work with exceptions for late notices (medical, surprise births) — submit as soon as you can.

Devin (Eng Mgr): Thanks, looks reasonable. I'll flag this in my 1:1s and remind the team to hit the ack.

Mica (People Ops): Thanks everyone. If you have a specific edge case (relocation, visa-dependent travel, or cross-country adoption), DM HR or drop a note here and we'll loop in legal/finance as needed. :wave:
